meta.title: SudoCut — sudo rm the boring parts.
meta.description: SudoCut removes the boring parts from long spoken footage. Join the closed-beta waitlist.

home.title: Four hours of footage. One story. Ninety seconds of work.
home.lede: SudoCut takes long, raw footage and hands back a cut worth keeping. AI strips the fillers, fumbles, silences, and NG takes. You keep the calls that matter, and finish in your own editor with FCPXML/SRT export. AI proposes. You decide.

proof.label: Blind test result
proof.detail: The same footage, cut twice. Once by a human editor, once by SudoCut. Shipped side by side, nobody called which was which.

chore.label: The chore — we remove it
chore.copy: Fillers, fumbles, dead air, tangents, retakes. Hours of cutting nobody's creativity lives in.

story.label: The story — you keep it
story.copy: Pacing, tone, what stays in. The last 20% is the creative work, and it stays yours.

example.after: . Nothing you wanted is gone. An illustration, not a promise.

about.title: Editing is the work. Scrubbing dead air isn't.
about.ledeBefore: Every long-form creator does the same low-value chore by hand: cutting fillers, fumbles, silences, tangents, NG takes. It's slow, repetitive, and nobody's creativity lives there. So we

one.title: The chore is universal.
one.copy: Solo YouTubers, podcast and interview editors, lecture makers, talk-heavy streamers. Everyone with raw footage pays the same hours before the real edit can start. That payment is not craft. It's tax.

two.title: The last 20% is the work.
two.copy: AI strips the boring 80%. Pacing, tone, and the final call stay with the creator, because that's where the creativity lives. AI proposes; humans decide. Every cut we make is a suggestion, never a shipment.

three.title: Your tools finish it.
three.copy: We export editor-ready FCPXML and SRT, so the cut lands in the editor you already use. No new timeline to learn, no lock-in. Less footage. More story.

proof.label: The proof in full
proof.detail: We shipped the same footage cut twice — once by a human editor, once by SudoCut — and put the two versions in front of viewers side by side. Nobody could call which was which. That evidence is why SudoCut is a product, not a pitch.

team.title: How the work gets decided.
team.lede: The roster isn't cleared for publication yet, so this page carries what can be published: the rules we decide by. Four of them. They cover most arguments.

one.title: We are not artists.
one.copy: There is art in editing. Our part of it isn't the art. We remove a chore so the creator's part can start sooner, and we don't confuse the two.

two.title: Direction over perfection.
two.copy: A cut that ships this week beats a perfect pipeline next year. We pick a direction, move, and let real footage correct us.

three.title: Honesty over polish.
three.copy: If the cut is wrong, we say it's wrong. Demos show real footage and real numbers, including the ones that don't flatter us.

four.title: AI proposes, humans decide.
four.copy: Every cut SudoCut makes is a suggestion on a timeline the creator still owns. The moment the tool decides instead of proposing, we've built the wrong product.

roster.label: Roster placeholder
roster.why: Names and faces land here once cleared. Until then, the four rules above are the team.
